candidates.angle: tigertime: catalyst timing on the corrected arena (TIGER track). The overlay de-risks into each public print and re-risks after it: half the long, and so half the hedge, on the close before a print that was announced at least announceLead days ahead; normal size again at the print's close.
candidates.hypothesis:
A premise in the brief needs correcting. RECOMMENDED_TIGER at 1d672c1 does NOT lean in ahead of prints: it inherits preEventDays 0, so preEventMult is inert and the book carries full size through every print.

Economics. The arena's prints are zero-mean gaps (CatalystEvent mean 0, vol 3-12%). The primary is the name that was most volatile on days 0-59, so its prints are large: the RMS print-day return is about 9%, against 2.8% on a normal day, and the book carries about 0.6 of its long into a print. A gamma=3 investor's cost of carrying a gap grows with the SQUARE of the size held through it. The round trip to shed it (20 bps on the long plus 5 bps x beta on the hedge, out and back) grows only LINEARLY. Halving therefore removes 3/4 of the gap variance for half the round trip; going flat pays the other half of the cost for the last 1/4. Leaning in is the same trade with the sign flipped, so it pays only if the book can sign the print. The rule is point-in-time: it reads only eventDistances(announceLead). The hedge is sized off the long, so the book stays beta-neutral through the gap.

EXPECTED effect over all research seeds 1-9999 (9,999 worlds, paired against the current code):
- Half into the print (this proposal): tiger CE +0.43 pp [90% +0.31, +0.56] (t=5.6); maxDD -1.08 pp (t=-41); tiger Sharpe -0.030; mean exposure unchanged (+0.001). It is NOT deleveraging.
- Flat into the print: +0.13 pp [-0.13, +0.39], maxDD -1.78 pp. The round trips (+0.82% of NAV per year) eat the gain.
- Lean in 1.5x on the eve: -0.81 pp [-0.90, -0.72], maxDD +0.82 pp. Lean in 1.5x for 5 days: -1.28 pp on 3001-4000 and -0.87 pp on dev, maxDD +1.0..1.2 pp.
- Cut sized by the gamma/cost optimum w* = 2c/(gamma*sigmaJ^2): +0.34 pp with sigmaJ estimated from the name's past prints (point-in-time), and +0.50 pp even with the latent sigmaJ (an oracle bound, research only). Sizing each name's cut is worth at most ~0.1 pp over a flat half.
- 'Re-risk after' done by excluding print days from the trailing vol: -0.49 pp, maxDD +0.72 pp. It sits exactly on the uniform-deleveraging line, so it is exposure, not timing.
- Break-even: an expected print return of about +0.4% (half-minus-off CE is +0.07 pp at mu=+0.35% and -0.08 pp at mu=+0.5%) would make carrying full size worth it again.

HONEST POWER CAVEAT: each world's CE swings with the signs of its ~3 realized prints, so the per-world SD of the paired difference is about 8 pp. In 49 disjoint 200-world blocks of research seeds:
- the CE gain was significant (90%) in 9 of 49 blocks, positive in 39, significantly negative in 0;
- maxDD fell significantly in 49 of 49.
Expect a sealed 200-world block to confirm the utility gain only about 1 time in 5. The robust, block-level effect is the drawdown (about -1.0..-1.4 pp).

Tiger Sharpe falls about 0.03 on average. Two causes: the round-trip cost (without costs the Sharpe change is -0.009 while CE rises +0.80 pp), and the overlay's negative mean excess return, where lower variance makes a negative Sharpe more negative.

Simulator-harvest check: with prints off, the rule is inert (no gain, no loss). It uses only the documented print schedule, not a generator quirk.
reviewProblems: RISK GUARD (Sharpe) is right at the limit and will fail on about half of sealed blocks. Over all 9,999 research seeds, paired against 1d672c1, the tiger Sharpe change is -0.0302 [90% -0.0348, -0.0255]. That is already past the 0.03 limit on average. In 49 disjoint 200-world research blocks, the Sharpe fall is more than 0.03 in 24 of them (min -0.081, median -0.0297, max +0.022). The CE 90% lower bound is above 0 AND the guard holds in only 9 of 49 blocks (about 18%), so block A is more likely to be lost to the guard than won. On the standard research block 1-200 the guard holds: CE +0.96 pp [+0.05, +1.88], maxDD -1.24 pp, Sharpe -0.002. The maxDD half of the guard never binds: maxDD falls significantly in 49 of 49 blocks and rises in none. About two-thirds of the Sharpe cost is round-trip cost. With costBps and hedgeCostBps at 0, half vs off gives Sharpe -0.009 and CE +0.815 pp.

The researcher's simulator-harvest check proves nothing. 'With prints off the rule is inert' holds by construction: with no event schedule, a timing rule never fires. The useful check keeps the schedule and changes the gap. With the generator's print vol halved (1.5-6% instead of 3-12%, same seeds, rule on vs off), the rule LOSES -0.20 pp [-0.27, -0.12]. With gaps set to 0 but the schedule kept, it loses -0.31 pp [-0.36, -0.25] (pure round-trip cost). Its sign therefore depends on the arena's hard-coded print-size range and on the hard-coded mean 0. The break-even is confirmed: print mean +0.4% gives -0.01 pp [-0.13, +0.12], and +0.2% gives +0.23 pp. I do not judge this a loop-4-style harvest. The rule reads only a public schedule, there is no deterministic return pattern to exploit, and the argument that gap variance costs quadratically while the round trip costs linearly holds in general. The arena's Tiger primary is also by design the most volatile name, like the Luckin case. Still, the flat 0.5 cut is tuned to the generator's print sizes. The researcher's print-vol-sized cut (+0.34 pp claimed) would hold up better for names with small prints.

The new RECOMMENDED_TIGER doc comment reports the drawdown and utility effects but not the Sharpe cost (about -0.03, which sits on the risk-guard limit), nor that the rule loses money when prints are small relative to the round-trip cost. Minor doc gap.

Knock-on change, not a failure: services/orchestrator/src/agenthire-demo.ts runs RECOMMENDED_TIGER on arena seed 3. The PM path now stops out at day 86 (dd 20.1%) instead of day 84 (21.2%). The demo's 'the ladder stopped the PM out' check still holds, but the committed apps/web/public agenthire snapshot or receipts would differ if regenerated.
candidates.reviewSummary:
I found none of the listed rejection grounds, so ok=true. The real risk is the Sharpe half of the risk guard, which this change breaches on average. Tested in scratch worktrees /tmp/loop-review-5-tigertime/wt (diff applied) and /tmp/loop-review-5-tigertime/base (1d672c1).

Integrity checks:
- **Applies and builds.** `git apply --check` is clean against 1d672c1. The typecheck passes. `npm test` passes 276/276, lab 66/66, web 59/59.
- **No arena or judge edits, no weakened tests.** The diff only changes `RECOMMENDED_TIGER` (preEventDays 1, preEventMult 0.5), fixes the doc comment (removes a duplicated hedge line) and adds 4 tests.
- **The premise is correct.** At 1d672c1, `RECOMMENDED_TIGER` inherits preEventDays 0, so the pre-event multiplier does nothing.
- **Point-in-time.** The rule reads only `until[t]` from `eventDistances(n, events, announceLead)`. I checked the timing in real arena worlds. `generateMarket` adds the print jump to tick e.tick, which is panel return day e.tick+1 = event t. Only the weight held into that day is halved, decided at close t-1. Size comes back at the print's close, and the hedge is halved with the long.
- **The tests guard against look-ahead.** I injected a look-ahead mutation (halve only when r[t+1] < 0). Five tests caught it, including the new eve test, the public-print test and the NO LOOK-AHEAD test (forks at 291, 292, 460).
- **No hard-coded seed values; not a structure claim.**

Headline numbers reproduce exactly over research seeds 1-9999, paired against the base:

| | CE (pp) | maxDD (pp) | Sharpe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Half into the print (this diff) | +0.432 [+0.306, +0.558], t=5.63 | -1.075 | -0.0302 |
| Flat into the print | +0.13 [-0.13, +0.39] | -1.78 | not checked |
| Half, no trading costs | +0.815 | not checked | -0.009 |

The robustness check at 200-world blocks also reproduces: CE is significant in 9 of 49 blocks, positive in 39, significantly negative in 0, and maxDD falls significantly in all 49. Mean exposure is 0.601 vs 0.599 (seeds 1-500), so this is not deleveraging. Print-day RMS return is 9.7% against 2.8% on other days.

Risk guard:
- **Block 1-200: holds.** CE +0.96 pp [+0.05, +1.88], maxDD -1.24 pp, Sharpe -0.002.
- **Across all research seeds: Sharpe fails.** The mean Sharpe fall is 0.0302, just past the 0.03 limit. It exceeds 0.03 in 24 of 49 blocks. The CE lower bound is above 0 AND the guard holds in only 9 of 49 blocks, about 18%. Expect the sealed judge to throw this out on the Sharpe guard about half the time.

Robustness beyond the researcher's check:
- **Their 'inert with prints off' test is empty.** With no event schedule the rule can never fire.
- **Keeping the schedule but shrinking the prints flips the sign.** With print vol halved the rule loses -0.20 pp [-0.27, -0.12]. With the gaps set to 0 it loses -0.31 pp (pure round-trip cost).
- **Break-even confirmed.** A print mean of +0.4% gives -0.01 pp; +0.2% gives +0.23 pp.
- **My judgement: not a harvest.** The rule uses a public schedule and the economics (gap cost grows with the square of size, round-trip cost linearly) hold in general. But the flat 0.5 cut is tuned to the generator's 3-12% print sizes. A cut sized by the name's print volatility would hold up better for names with small prints.

One knock-on effect: `services/orchestrator/src/agenthire-demo.ts` (seed 3) still stops the PM out, now at day 86 instead of 84. A regenerated snapshot under `apps/web/public` would differ; no test depends on it.

Scripts: `/tmp/loop-review-5-tigertime/tiger-eval.mts`, `exp.mts`, `pair.mjs`, `blocks.mjs`, `align.mts`, `demo-ladder.mts`.

candidates.angle: operatorlift: (G) structure. This is the second attempt at loop 4's rejected fix. The operator cap is now a ceiling kept separate from each name's own size, and the name holds the smaller of the two.
candidates.hypothesis:
Invariant, designed first: for every live name at every tick, min(L, cutFactor x fullSize) <= budget <= L. Here L is what the name holds under its own rules alone: the allocator's target under the rebalance band, its own ladder cuts, and crowding cuts. Where no crowding limit binds, L equals the name's budget in the same book with every operator label removed.

Why the earlier designs failed: loops 3 and 4 kept a single number (capital) and decided each cut on that number. Once a cap is lifted, that number no longer remembers what the name's own rules would give it, so a later ladder cut or re-cap compounds to cutFactor^2. Loop 3 also had the opposite fault: a name the ladder had already cut was not cut again (it was already at the ceiling), which left it above what its own ladder allows.

The design keeps two numbers per held name (OperatorSizing, in allocator.ts):
- own: moved only by the name's own rules. Reallocation moves it to its own target under the band; a ladder cut multiplies it by cutFactor; a crowding cut sets it to the absolute level the crowding check chose; a stop sets it to 0.
- ceiling: cutFactor x fullSize, set by the cap and by any re-cap. It is refreshed at each reallocation while the cap is in force. After a lift it stays until the next reallocation re-sizes the name. Loop 3 also never grew a lifted name before then, so this changes no capital path.

The budget written to the tree is exactly min(own, ceiling). Operator events (cap, re-cap, lift) never touch own, so the band holds by construction for any number of names per operator and any order of events. Names that no ceiling holds follow the old code path exactly. I made no return claim: utility, max drawdown and Sharpe are unchanged to within about 0.001 pp.
reviewProblems: Non-blocking: the proof is only against the unlabelled book where no crowding limit binds. With crowding on, a held name's crowding cut is solved on its capped holding and lands on its own size. The arena test (arena-operator-sizing.test.ts) therefore checks the band against the book's own `ownSize` record, not against the blind book, so that part is partly self-referential. The README/CENTER-BOOK text says this, so it is not a hidden gap.

Non-blocking: the budget can sit up to CEILING_SLACK (1e-9 relative, about 1 micro-USDC) above the own size. My stress run with rebalanceBand 0 and 0.5 on seed 23, name o0n2 at t=39, gave a budget of 111366.898822 against an own size of 111366.898821. The cause is that `cutTo` does not write within the slack after a cap rounded the budget up. The docs' 'to the micro-USDC' caveat covers this.

Non-blocking: capped names are now re-sized at every reallocation with no rebalance band on top (the budget follows cutFactor x fullTarget exactly), so there are more REALLOCATE writes and decisions for capped names than at 1d672c1. This is intentional, so that the cap binds at the new full size, but it is extra churn.

Non-blocking, stale docs and dead code: the nextCounterpartyCaps docstring still says the cap and ladder 'compound neither in size (see `cutToCeiling`)', but the book no longer uses cutToCeiling. `allocate`'s counterpartyMultiplier path is also no longer used by the book; it is documented and still unit-tested (allocator test 212).

Non-blocking: the claim that performance is 'unchanged to within about 0.001 pp' is slightly understated. Allocator utility moved -0.0032 pp on seeds 1-200 and -0.0022 pp on seeds 3001-3200. It is still negligible, and Tiger is bit-identical.
candidates.reviewSummary:
I recommend accepting this diff. It applies cleanly to 1d672c1, and its tests prove the guarantee it claims.

**Setup.** The staged diff in .claude/worktrees/wf_77c9e3c4-660-4 has the same blob hashes as the proposed diff. I saved it as /tmp/loop-review-5-operatorlift/patch.diff and applied it to a scratch worktree at /tmp/loop-review-5-operatorlift/wt; `git apply --check` passed. A second, untouched worktree at /tmp/loop-review-5-operatorlift/base is the baseline.

**Tests and typecheck.** Typecheck (`tsc -b`) passes. `npm test` passes all 278 tests, 0 failing. That is 6 new tests: 5 in packages/swarm/src/operator-sizing.test.ts and 1 in packages/lab/src/arena-operator-sizing.test.ts.

**Rule checks.**
- No existing test file is modified; the three package.json files only add the two new test files.
- The arena and judge files are untouched: arena.ts, arena-cli.ts, loop-judge.mjs and worktree-setup.sh.
- The mechanism reads no future information. `holds` and `nextSizing` only use the current tree budget, the current allocator target or full size, the ladder state and the operator caps at the decision tick.
- No seed-specific values are in the mechanism. Seeds appear only in test fixtures (research seeds 1–40, plus the scripted market's seed).
- Agents are not identified by strategy class.

**Is the base bug real?** Yes. I ran the proposal's scripted roster on unpatched 1d672c1:
- **Loop 3 compounding:** name y (lifted, then cut by its own ladder) ends at 250k with labels, against 500k without.
- **Cap weakening the ladder:** name w (cut, restored, capped, cut again) ends at 500k, against 250k without.

With the patch, x, y and w all match the unlabelled book (500k, 500k and 250k).

**Adversarial stress test.** I copied the proposal's book harness into a scratch file (since deleted) and ran crowding-free random books, each with and without operator labels:
- Seeds 41–240 on the default policy.
- 60–80 seeds each for these variants: cutFactor 0.3 and 0.7; rebalanceBand 0 and 0.5; rebalanceEvery 1; rebalanceEvery 20 over 300 ticks; 5 operators with more frequent jumps; warmup 5.

That is about 580k live ticks, with hundreds of re-caps and hundreds of ladder cuts on capped names. Results:
- Full sizes match between the two books everywhere.
- The labels move no ladder.
- The book's own size equals the unlabelled budget everywhere.
- `min(own, cutFactor x full) <= budget <= own` holds everywhere, except one 1-micro-USDC rounding case (listed under problems).

**Test quality.** The property test's reference model largely mirrors `nextSizing`, so on its own it proves little. The book-level comparisons with and without labels (the scripted book plus 40 random books) are independent, and they fail on the base behaviour.

**Risk guard, 200 worlds per block, patch minus base (research seeds only):**

| Block | Utility | Sharpe | maxDD | Base maxDD | Base Sharpe |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seeds 1–200 | -0.0032 pp | -0.00028 | +0.0003 pp | 7.122% | 1.2948 |
| Seeds 3001–3200 | -0.0022 pp | -0.00017 | +0.0009 pp | 7.488% | 1.1560 |

Both blocks are far inside the limits (maxDD rise of at most 0.5 pp, Sharpe fall of at most 0.03). Tiger's metrics are identical to the base.

The remaining problems are all non-blocking:
- The guarantee is only proved against the unlabelled book where no crowding limit binds; the docs say so.
- The budget can sit up to about 1 micro-USDC above the own size, from rounding.
- Capped names are now re-sized at every reallocation, with no rebalance band.
- One docstring still refers to `cutToCeiling`, which the book no longer uses.
- The researcher's "about 0.001 pp" understates the actual -0.002 to -0.003 pp utility change.

The main files are packages/swarm/src/book.ts and packages/swarm/src/allocator.ts. The run outputs are in /tmp/loop-review-5-operatorlift/: base-1.json, wt-1.json, base-3001.json, wt-3001.json and test.log.

candidates.angle: Wildcard (A): score each agent's record on ALPHA, not on its raw return. Before the allocator ranks records, it takes out the part the market explains. This is the appraisal ratio of Jensen and Treynor-Black, and it is how pod shops pay PMs: on idiosyncratic (factor-neutral) P&L. It is one economically motivated, point-in-time change to how (A) resizes reservations. It does not deploy more capital and does not loosen any limit.
candidates.hypothesis:
The allocator ranks agents by shrunk Sharpe over the last year of record. A raw record mixes two things: the agent's alpha, and its beta times whatever the market did in that window. The market's run over the window is not the agent's skill; an index fund would have earned it too. So in a year when the market trended, raw Sharpe pays capital to agents that happened to be positioned with the market, trend followers above all. Stripping the market's part (a single-index OLS on the equal-weighted return of the fund's universe, over the same window) should rank agents on evidence of skill. Capital should move from zero-edge agents that rode the market to agents with idiosyncratic edge. At the same capital at work, that should give a higher Sharpe, higher utility and a lower drawdown. The gain should be largest in worlds where the market trended most.

Evidence, all on research seeds and measured, not designed from the generator. I read only market.ts's header doc comment and its interfaces, not its dynamics.
(1) Diagnostic before any code (seeds 2001–2200): in the cross-section, the alpha score predicts agents' 20-tick forward returns better than raw Sharpe. The mean correlation is 0.0715 vs 0.0645, with a paired difference of +0.0070 ± 0.0023. A score-weighted portfolio earns +1.2 pp/yr more per unit.
(2) Where the capital moves (style tags used only for diagnosis, never by the allocator): trend agents' mean capital share falls from 4.02% to 3.59%. Their share of the worst drawdown's loss falls from 16.2% to 13.3%. Mean-reversion agents gain share, and skilled agents are unchanged.
(3) The mechanism check holds. Pooled over 750 research worlds, split into terciles by how much the market trended in the world (|annualized Sharpe of the equal-weighted index|): utility +0.15 / +0.16 / +0.34 pp and maxDD −0.02 / −0.13 / −0.15 pp from calm to trending. Crowd vs no-crowd worlds gain about the same (pooled ≈ +0.22 vs +0.21 pp), so this is not a harvest of the crowd, crash or aftershock.
(4) Fund-level alternatives I tried offline first were null (see notes).

Point-in-time: the market return of tick t is pushed with the agents' records at the end of tick t. A reallocation at tick t therefore regresses records through t−1 on the market through t−1. allocate refuses a market series whose length is not exactly the records' length.
reviewProblems: NON-BLOCKING: on the docs' own 20-seed example the center book's mean Sharpe falls from 0.50 to 0.43. I confirmed it with `npm run demo:swarm` in the candidate worktree, and every changed number in README and CENTER-BOOK matches that output. The drop is disclosed honestly. Over example seeds 1–200 I reproduced the researcher's paired figures: Sharpe −0.016 ± 0.037 and maxDD −0.15 ± 0.10 pp. So the 20-seed drop is noise, but the README headline now says 'lower mean Sharpe' where it used to say 'same'.

NON-BLOCKING: claim (3) only partly replicates. The researcher said the utility gain is largest in trending worlds (+0.15 / +0.16 / +0.34 pp). On my 1,200 worlds, split into terciles by the equal-weighted index's |annualized Sharpe|, the utility gain is +0.26 ± 0.15, +0.15 ± 0.18 and +0.22 ± 0.21 pp, with no trend gradient. The drawdown gradient does replicate: maxDD −0.04, −0.12 and −0.21 pp from calm to trending. Crowd and no-crowd worlds gain about the same (+0.19 vs +0.26 pp), so this is not a crowd harvest.

nullResults.angle: tigerladder (loop 5, TIGER track): scale the Tiger overlay's drawdown rungs (cut 15%, stop 30%) by the vol the book runs, measured up to its high-water mark, with a floor and a ceiling. This is loop 1's allocator fix carried over to the single-name overlay. RESULT: NULL. No diff is proposed.
nullResults.hypothesis:
Hypothesis tested: a fixed-percentage ladder mis-prices drawdowns across books that run different vol, as it did for the allocator's agents in loop 1. If so, rungs in vol units (sigma measured up to the high-water mark, so the losses being judged cannot move their own limit) should stop fewer books on noise, or protect low-vol books sooner, and do better than uniform deleveraging.

Why it fails here (NULL on both blocks):

1) The overlay is already vol-targeted (35% on the long), so its risk is compressed. Its unit-return vol (every gate but the ladder) is 22.8 / 33.3 / 37.1% at the 10th / 50th / 90th percentiles on dev (27.3 / 34.1 / 37.4% on check). The name's own vol is 36 / 50 / 65%. A fixed-% ladder on a vol-targeted book is already close to a risk-scaled ladder. Loop 1's agents' vols differed several-fold.

2) Drawdowns in sigma units carry no more information than drawdowns in percent. Test: the no-ladder book on dev, 32,200 closes, forward 20-day return in sigma units.
   - By drawdown %: +0.114 near the high to -0.111 at 30% or more.
   - By drawdown in sigma: +0.126 to -0.114.
   - The spread is the same, and the risk-scaled drawdown ranks books no better.

3) The name has no edge (overlay Sharpe about -0.2), so in this arena every ladder only deleverages. The tiger track's CE rises monotonically as exposure falls:
   - vol target 0.37 / 0.33 / 0.31 / 0.29 gives -0.71 / +0.60 / +1.01 / +1.82 pp on dev
   - it gives -0.57 / +0.80 / +1.88 pp on check (0.37 / 0.33 / 0.31).
   Loop 1's gain came from not stopping skilled agents with positive expected returns. That mechanism is absent here.

Variants (all point-in-time: the ladder at close t reads only unit returns up to the last high-water mark, at or before t; a fork test on 40 arena worlds x 3 fork points, 10,240 weights, moved nothing):
- (a) l1, the loop-1 analogue, widen only: stop = clamp(30% x sigma/20%, 30%, 40%) = max(30%, 1.5 sigma) capped at 40%; the cut moves in proportion.
- (b) vt-ref, two-sided: rungs set for a book at the 35% vol target; stop = clamp(30% x sigma/35%, 15%, 40%).
- (c) neutral: as (b) with the reference at the median unit vol, 33.3%. This is a diagnostic, run on dev only.
- (d) fix0.40: the literal "name's vol" reading. 1.5 x name vol is at least 54% in more than 90% of worlds, so that reading collapses to the 40% ceiling, i.e. a 20% cut and 40% stop.

nullResults.angle: Residual scoring (ALLOCATOR track): rank each agent on its record net of the book's common factor instead of its raw Sharpe. NULL RESULT, so no diff is submitted.
nullResults.hypothesis:
Herders and trend agents earn a Sharpe that is mostly the crowd's run-up, and their records overlap the skilled pickers'. The candidate (v1) scored each agent on its Sharpe net of what the rest of the book already earns: score = S − max(0,ρ)·max(0,S_peers). Here S_peers is the Sharpe of a leave-one-out, equal-risk index of the other live agents' records over the same recordWindow. Each record is divided by its own vol, so the index is scale-invariant and no single levered book dominates it. This equals the residual (r − β·f) mean per unit of the agent's TOTAL risk, and it is the marginal-Sharpe test S > ρ·S_peers. The haircut only ever takes credit away. It is point-in-time: it reads only unitReturns up to t−1. The hypothesis was that capital would move from factor riders to pickers.

Finding: the haircut orders the styles correctly. At t=150 on dev seeds (survivors) the mean haircut is: herd 1.36 of S 2.14, trend 0.69 of 1.28, skilled 0.48 of 1.79, noise 0.13 of 0.98, meanrev 0.07 of 1.63. But in the real book it buys nothing, for three reasons.
(1) Herders are already starved by the position-based crowding limits and multiplicity: 3% of NAV, and their net PnL is positive (+0.23% of NAV).
(2) The largest no-edge bucket is noise, at 8% of NAV. Noise is uncorrelated with everyone, so the residual cannot touch it. The capital freed from trend (7.6→6.55% of NAV) flows pro rata, partly to noise (8.0→8.2%), and total capital at work falls 46.6→45.4%.
(3) Pickers share skill (they correlate about 0.17 with each other), so a peer index charges them about 0.5 Sharpe for each other's edge. That is shared alpha, not crowd.

In an idealized re-allocation on the baseline records with no ladder and no crowd limits, the haircut does lift forward Sharpe (1.04→1.11). So it works as a substitute for position-based crowd limits, not as an addition to them.
